title: PDF body font size adapts to the longest positive dollar value on the four-tier scale, with fixed column widths
permissions_required: A user with Reports access who can open the Sales By Representative report.
preconditions: 1. You can produce (or seed) filtered views whose LONGEST formatted positive dollar value — checked across every value in the document, including the totals row — falls in different length brackets (for example, $1,234.56 = 9 characters vs $1,000,000.00 = 13 characters).
steps: 1. Download the Summary PDF for a view whose longest positive dollar value is 9 characters or fewer; note the body text size.
2. Repeat for views whose longest positive value is 10, 11, and 12-or-more characters (as far as seedable).
3. In each file, check whether any value overflows or wraps its column.
expected: 1. The body font follows the tier scale by the longest formatted positive dollar value in the document (totals included): 9 characters or fewer → 11px; 10 characters → 10px; 11 characters → 9px; 12 or more → 8px. 8px is the floor and 11px the ceiling.
2. Column widths are fixed for the worst case regardless of tier — the layout never breaks and no value overflows.
3. Both PDF formats adapt the same way.
design_ref: none - SPEC-ONLY (Report Suite has no designs yet)
notes: Exact pixel sizes need a PDF inspector or side-by-side comparison at VIU; verify the relative step-downs and the no-overflow guarantee at minimum.
